name: forgetting-things-in-front-of-kids
peak_moment: mid-conversation with own kids, realizes she's asked the same question twice
failed_solutions: nothing tried yet at time of the pain - this is the triggering moment, not a post-failure moment

cost.functional: loses track of daily tasks and conversations
cost.emotional: kids making her feel bad about herself, self-blame spiral
cost.social: kids notice and comment on it directly

identity_dimension: wants to be the mom who's present and sharp for her kids, fears becoming the forgetful/checked-out mom
dream_state: kids notice the opposite change unprompted ('mom you don't seem like...')

voc_quotes.text: I was forgetting every single thing. Like the kids were literally making me feel really bad about myself.
the kids have noticed, they're like, Wow, mom, you don't seem like you're not asking me the same thing

name: not-more-caffeine-a-better-routine
peak_moment: sitting with a coffee, staring at the same unanswered email for 20 minutes
failed_solutions: assuming it's just a personal rut/laziness

cost.functional: tasks pile up despite being awake and caffeinated
cost.emotional: feels like fighting her own brain all day

identity_dimension: wants to feel like herself despite an unchanged chaotic life (messy kitchen, long to-do list still exist)
dream_state: more focused, 'more like myself' - explicitly NOT a claim that life gets easier, just that the internal fight stops

voc_quotes.text: I kept telling myself I just need another cup of coffee. But for me, it wasn't more caffeine that I needed. It was a better routine.
it's not like my life suddenly got less chaotic... but I don't feel like I'm fighting my own brain. I feel more focused and honestly, more like myself.

name: hair-loss-as-the-visible-tell-of-stress
peak_moment: noticing hair volume in the shower drain, then on the brush, then 'everywhere'

cost.functional: visible physical change she can't hide
cost.emotional: identity threat - 'hits pretty different' because it's visible vs. internal fatigue
cost.social: implicit - hair loss is publicly visible in a way fatigue isn't

identity_dimension: was trying to fix a surface symptom without realizing the root cause was systemic (stress response), reframes self from 'broken' to 'undersupported'
dream_state: addressing the internal stress response rather than chasing surface hair fixes

voc_quotes.text: I started noticing more hairs in the shower first, and then on my brush, and then kind of everywhere.
I was trying to fix something on the outside that was being caused on the inside.

name: weight-loss-exhaustion-not-hunger
peak_moment: mid-workout, noticing the workout itself feels harder than it used to
failed_solutions: continuing to diet/exercise harder without addressing energy directly

cost.emotional: frustration that discipline (diet, gym) isn't 'working' the way expected

identity_dimension: wants to be someone whose effort translates to results; fears the effort itself becoming impossible to sustain

voc_quotes.text: The most frustrating part of my weight-loss journey wasn't hunger. It was the exhaustion.
